clue.text: Disappointments of animated film series

parts.note: Up is the 2009 Pixar animated film
series can be plural, and several series are sets

explanation.surface: A cartoon franchise has let its fans down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film series' reads as one unit, but the split falls after 'film': the animated film is one piece and 'series' is read as a plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Upsets are setbacks or unexpected defeats, things that let people down, so they serve as synonyms for letdowns.

clue.text: Quietly be indebted to Greek character and work for energetic person

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly
to owe is to be indebted
rho is a letter of the Greek alphabet
to use something is to work it

explanation.surface: Someone quietly in debt to a Greek and putting in hard graft for a dynamic colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' looks like a person in the story; here it is a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A powerhouse is a person of great drive and vigour.

clue.text: Some of sect in kingdom's uprising closely unite

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading from the bottom upward, so the letters run backwards
only some of the letters are wanted, a run lifted from inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of 'sect', all of 'in' and the start of 'kingdom'

explanation.surface: Part of a religious sect rises up against the crown and its members band together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uprising' looks like a rebellion in the kingdom; in a down clue it tells you to read the hidden letters bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: To knit is to join firmly together, as broken bones knit or a community knits together.

clue.text: Body of artists knocking back a litre, alcohol's drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests something reeling, so the letters are rearranged
knocking back a drink takes it away, so those letters are removed

parts.note: the word alcohol with its S

explanation.surface: Artists downing a litre, getting drunk on spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocking back' reads as drinking, but here it takes letters away before 'drunk' rearranges what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A school is a group of painters sharing a style or teacher, like the Venetian school.

clue.text: Old language of Spain regularly used on border with resistance mounting

indicators.note: in a down clue one thing put on another sits above it, so the first part comes before the rest
at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters

indicators.note: in a down clue mounting means climbing, so one letter shifts higher up the word

parts.note: a skirt is an edging or border, as in the skirts of a town
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: An ancient tongue from Spain turns up on a frontier where opposition is growing.
explanation.walkthrough: The R already inside the border word climbs one place in this down clue, turning SKIRT into SKRIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanskrit is the classical language of ancient India, the liturgical tongue of Hinduism and an ancestor of many Indian languages.

clue.text: Thrown shot, bulls-eye's first hit

parts.note: a shot is a go, a try

indicators.note: the first means only the opening letter of that word is taken

parts.note: the initial letter
to hit is to smack, here in the past tense

explanation.surface: A darts or archery commentator: the throw landed, the first bullseye scored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thrown' looks like part of the darts scene; it is the definition, in its sense of disconcerted.
explanation.definitionFit: Gobsmacked is British slang for utterly astonished, and being thrown is being disconcerted or caught off guard.

clue.text: Dig US rapper endlessly

indicators.note: without its ends, so the first and last letters of the rapper's name are dropped

parts.note: Eminem is the American rapper Marshall Mathers

explanation.surface: A dig at an American rapper who goes on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' strips the E and the M off the ends of EMINEM, leaving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To mine is to dig into the ground to extract ore or coal.

clue.text: Learner in shift working for club

indicators.note: one element is placed inside another

parts.note: to budge is to shift slightly
L is the learner-driver plate
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A trainee on a work shift at a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' looks like a nightclub or society; it is the heavy stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A bludgeon is a thick stick with a heavy end used as a weapon, which is one meaning of club.

clue.text: Ancient civilisation in hope to turn foreign agents

indicators.note: turning things over and around changes their order

parts.note: the letters of both words taken together
the CIA is the US agency for intelligence abroad

explanation.surface: An old society hopes to win over spies from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word placing the civilisation in hope; it is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoenicia was the seafaring trading culture of the ancient eastern Mediterranean coast, in modern Lebanon.

clue.text: Abandoning wings, Conservatives left for recess

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its outer letters, and these are abandoned

parts.note: Tories are members of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Conservative MPs, deserting the party's wings, leave for the parliamentary recess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoning wings' drops the T and S from TORIES to give ORIE, and L follows. 'recess' hints at Parliament's holiday, but it is an alcove.
explanation.definitionFit: An oriel is a bay window projecting from an upper storey, forming a recess in the room.

clue.text: Chosen extremely retro type of music

parts.note: the elect are those chosen

indicators.note: at the extremes, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone has picked a very old-fashioned musical style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely retro' looks like very old-fashioned; it means the extreme letters of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Electro is a genre of electronic dance music from the early 1980s, mixing funk with drum machines.

clue.text: Hang American exhaust brackets

indicators.note: brackets enclose what sits between them

parts.note: to exhaust money or energy is to spend it
US is the standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A US mechanic hangs up exhaust brackets in a garage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brackets' looks like a noun for the exhaust fittings; it is a verb meaning encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspend something is to hang it from above, so it is dangling.

clue.text: Organiser that woman used to pen about matter half-heartedly

indicators.note: to pen is to shut in, as animals are enclosed in a fold

parts.note: she'd, short for she would, as in what she used to do
c (circa) means about

indicators.note: with the heart lacking, so the central letter goes

parts.note: an ulcer is a sore that discharges matter, or pus

explanation.surface: A personal assistant: she used to write about business, without much enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Matter' looks like the subject being written about; read medically it is pus, and a sore producing it loses its central C.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheduler is someone or something that draws up timetables, an arranger of appointments and plans.

clue.text: Toxic nature shown two seconds beyond time limit

indicators.note: past or after, so one part follows the other

parts.note: a deadline is a time limit
S is the abbreviation for second, twice

explanation.surface: Someone's poisonous temperament shows when they overrun a deadline by two seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a rare form: deadliness from deadly, not from deadline, though it contains the time limit word.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadliness is the quality of being lethal, and a poison's toxic nature is its capacity to kill.

clue.text: Full minute shifting back in tree

indicators.note: moving back means a letter slides one place further along the word

parts.note: the maple is a tree
M is the abbreviation for minute

explanation.surface: A full minute spent swaying backwards in a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The M of the tree name moves back past the A, so MAPLE becomes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means plentiful or more than enough, so it describes a generous, abundant or substantial quantity.

clue.text: Not the plan being injured for athletic event

indicators.note: something injured is damaged and out of shape, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: the letters of all three words

explanation.surface: An athlete's injury was not part of the plan for the competition.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about a setback; the first three words supply exactly the ten letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: The pentathlon is a five-discipline contest, such as the modern pentathlon at the Olympics.

clue.text: Told where you'd find students get on transport

indicators.note: something told is spoken, so a word is taken by its sound

parts.note: students live in a hall of residence
to get on is to grow older, to age

explanation.surface: Students are given directions to where they can catch the bus.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech hall and haul sound alike; only the first part is said aloud, while 'get on' means grow old.
explanation.definitionFit: Haulage is the commercial carrying of goods by road, a kind of freight transport business.

clue.text: Nasty bears close to bobcat dens

indicators.note: to bear is to carry, so one part holds another

parts.note: hideous means very nasty or ugly

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is taken

parts.note: the final letter

explanation.surface: Fierce bears are living near a wildcat's lairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bears' looks like the animals, fitting the bobcat; it is a verb meaning carries.
explanation.definitionFit: A den is a secret hiding place, such as a criminals' den, so hideouts are synonyms.

clue.text: Request stony-hearted rogue to dispose of dosh

indicators.note: behaving like a rogue, out of order, so the remaining letters are rearranged
the letters of the money word are got rid of from the fodder before rearranging

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter by letter
taken as written; dosh is British slang for money

explanation.surface: A plea to a heartless crook to get rid of the cash.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters D, O, S and H out of STONY-HEARTED, leaving TNYEARTE, and 'rogue' rearranges those eight. Dosh is British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest appeal or plea, which is a kind of request.

clue.text: Assumed view Nancy's negative

parts.note: one's take on something is one's view
Nancy is a French city, and non is French for no

explanation.surface: It's assumed that Nancy takes a pessimistic view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nancy' looks like a woman's name; it is the city in north-eastern France, so its word for no is French.
explanation.definitionFit: To take on a role or responsibility is to assume it, so both mean accepted or adopted.

clue.text: Stay mad ignoring mother successfully

indicators.note: ignoring means the letters for mother are passed over and left out of mad

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
well means successfully, as in 'it went well'

explanation.surface: Advice to stay put, even if angry, and not mind what mother says.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell is to live or remain in a place, the verb sense of stay.

clue.text: Indirect hint hard to decipher overwhelming daughter

indicators.note: to overwhelm is to engulf, so one thing swallows another
deciphering means working letters into a new readable order

parts.note: the letters of both words
d is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A daughter is swamped by a vague, cryptic hint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hint' looks like part of the definition; the definition is just the first word, and 'hint hard' is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Third-hand information comes via intermediaries rather than straight from the source, so it is received indirectly.

clue.text: Rush home with virus unknown

indicators.note: placed alongside, so the parts sit next to each other

parts.note: someone at home is in
flu is caused by a virus
x is the algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Someone hurries home after catching a mystery bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rush home' reads as a command to hurry back; 'Rush' alone is a noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An influx is a sudden arrival of many people or things, a surge or flood.

clue.text: Knock wine over fancy bar area

indicators.note: knocked over means flipped, so the letters read the other way

parts.note: red is a type of wine

indicators.note: bar means except, so a letter is excluded

parts.note: a fancy is a notion or idea
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Someone knocks a glass of wine over in a smart bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock' looks like the cause of the spill; it is the definition, meaning criticise. 'Bar' looks like a pub but means except.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock is informal for disparaging or criticising, and to deride is to mock or ridicule.

clue.text: Fault spoilt coins: missing head

parts.note: food that has gone off is spoilt

indicators.note: the word loses its first letter

parts.note: pence are British coins

explanation.surface: A collector complains that some damaged coins are missing the monarch's head.
explanation.walkthrough: PENCE (coins) 'missing head' drops its P to give ENCE, after OFF (spoilt, as food goes off).
explanation.definitionFit: In sport an offence is an infringement of the rules, a fault committed by a player.

clue.text: Out of order having stomach upset

indicators.note: the stomach of a word is its middle, and in this down clue those middle letters are turned upside down

parts.note: form is order or arrangement, as in good form

explanation.surface: Someone is out of action with an upset stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: The stomach of FORM is its middle pair OR, which 'upset' turns into RO, giving F-RO-M. 'Out of' is the definition, in the sense of coming from somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: From and out of both mark a source or origin, as in made from wood or out of wood.

clue.text: Maybe primary suspect nicking article

indicators.note: to nick is to steal, so one piece takes another into itself

parts.note: to suspect something bad is to fear it
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: The prime suspect may be the one who stole the item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primary suspect' reads as a police phrase; 'Maybe primary' is the definition, as primaries are a type of feather.
explanation.definitionFit: Primaries are the main flight quills on a bird's wing tip, so a primary is an example of a feather.

clue.text: Cross mayor bringing up case of arson

indicators.note: the case of arson is its outer pair of letters, and the same pair at the end of the mayor's name is brought up to the top of this down entry

parts.note: Sadiq Khan is the Mayor of London

explanation.surface: An angry mayor raises a case of arson.
explanation.walkthrough: The case of arson is A and N, its outside letters; 'bringing up' moves that pair from the bottom of KHAN to the top, giving AN-KH.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankh is the ancient Egyptian looped cross, a hieroglyph meaning life.

clue.text: Old parts like this showing imperial measurements

indicators.note: to part something is to split it open, so another piece goes inside

parts.note: thus means in this way
o is a standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Old machine parts made in this style come in imperial sizes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old parts' reads as worn components; 'parts' is a verb. The answer could tempt you towards the archaic pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: A thou is a thousandth of an inch, a unit used by engineers working in imperial measures.

clue.text: Maybe quantity of 17 fight beside lake to feed amphibian

indicators.note: feeding puts something into a mouth, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: the toad is an amphibian

indicators.note: placed next to, so the parts sit side by side

parts.note: a ruck is a brawl or scrap
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A fight by a lake over feeding a frog.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to 17 Across, HAULAGE; a truckload is one possible amount of goods hauled.
explanation.definitionFit: A truckload is the amount a lorry carries, and haulage is moving goods by lorry.
